rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is empty, so the first experiment should test a multimodal baseline to assess if combining RNA and image data improves performance. This clarifies the potential benefit of multimodal approaches, which are central to the problem. Starting with a simple multimodal configuration (pca_n2000 RNA encoder, resnet50 image encoder, concat fusion) isolates the effect of modality combination without overcomplicating other design choices.

The existing evidence shows that config_016 (multimodal, concat fusion) achieves 52.7% accuracy. This experiment tests whether switching to weighted fusion (config_017) improves performance, isolating the effect of fusion strategy. It balances exploitation (building on multimodal approach) and exploration (testing fusion method), with minimal parameter changes to focus on a critical design choice.

Existing evidence shows multimodal singleprofile models with pca_n2000 and resnet50 achieve ~0.526 accuracy. This experiment tests multiprofile with avgpool aggregation (a key design choice not yet tested) while keeping RNA/image encoders consistent. It isolates the impact of profile setting and aggregation, which are critical for multimodal performance, and balances exploration of multiprofile benefits against the previous singleprofile baseline.

The existing evidence shows that config_018 (multimodal, multiprofile, avgpool, concat) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.6186). This experiment tests changing the fusion method from concat to weighted in the same multiprofile setup, isolating the effect of fusion strategy. It balances exploitation of the high-performing multiprofile configuration with exploration of fusion methods, which could further improve accuracy without altering other key components.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion (e.g., config_019) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.639). This experiment tests whether replacing the image encoder from resnet50 to imagenet_vit_l (a more powerful vision transformer) further improves performance, isolating the impact of the image encoder while keeping other parameters consistent. This is a focused exploration of a critical design choice with high potential for improvement.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile models with avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion (config_019) achieve the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests whether switching to transformer aggregation (a more complex method) while keeping other parameters the same could further improve performance. It isolates the effect of aggregation strategy, which is critical for model effectiveness, and builds on the promising direction of multiprofile and weighted fusion.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile models with weighted fusion and avgpool aggregation (e.g., config_019) achieve high accuracy. This experiment tests replacing avgpool with transformer aggregation and using imagenet_vit_l (a stronger image encoder) while retaining weighted fusion. It clarifies whether advanced aggregation methods and encoders can further improve performance, balancing exploration of key design choices with building on prior success.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal, multiprofile, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion yield high accuracy (e.g., config_019: 0.639). This experiment tests whether replacing the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 (a more sophisticated encoder) improves performance, isolating the impact of RNA representation. This balances exploitation of the current best setup with exploration of a key design choice, maximizing the chance of finding a higher accuracy configuration within the remaining budget.

The existing evidence shows that config_031 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, avgpool, weighted) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.6776). This experiment tests whether replacing the image encoder with imagenet_vit_l (a more advanced architecture) while keeping RNA encoder, aggregation, and fusion unchanged could further improve performance. This isolates the effect of the image encoder, a critical design choice, and leverages the strong prior evidence for scvi_n200 and weighted fusion.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 and imagenet_vit_l encoders, multiprofile, and weighted fusion (e.g., config_037) achieve high accuracy. This experiment tests transformer aggregation with weighted fusion, which could further improve performance by leveraging more sophisticated sequence modeling. It directly compares aggregation methods (avgpool vs. transformer) while keeping other components aligned, clarifying the impact of aggregation on performance.
